input:
We are losing perf PMU samples on our arm64 platform when using pseudo-NMI for the PMU overflow interrupt. Under heavy interrupt load, approximately 15-20% of expected PMU samples are missing compared to the same workload on x86 with hardware NMI.

perf stat comparison:
  Expected cycles samples (based on frequency): ~100,000
  Actual collected: 82,341 (17.7% loss)

dmesg:
  [   0.800] GICv3: pseudo-NMI enabled for PMU overflow (IRQ 23, priority=0x20)
  [   0.801] GICv3: normal IRQ priority=0x80, PMR threshold=0xF0

ftrace irq_handler_entry (sampled):
  irq_handler_entry: irq=23 name=arm-pmu
    read ICC_PMR_EL1 = 0x20  <-- PMR lowered by another pseudo-NMI handler
    PMU overflow IRQ masked by PMR! sample lost
    write ICC_PMR_EL1 = 0xF0  (restore)
  ---
  irq_handler_entry: irq=18 name=arch_timer
    in pseudo-NMI context, ICC_PMR_EL1 = 0x20
    PMU overflow at same priority, cannot nest
    duration: 1.2us (PMU sample window missed)

The PMU and arch_timer pseudo-NMIs share the same priority group (0x20). When the arch_timer pseudo-NMI handler is running, it lowers PMR to 0x20, masking the PMU overflow at the same priority. Is this a known limitation of Linux pseudo-NMI, and how do we assign different priorities to avoid the race?
